messages.subject: length frequency by sex with ggplot2
parts:
Dear all,


I would like to plot something like the example below with my fish length frequency data, disaggregated by sex but binned by length class (1 cm in most cases). Thus, each row of my data frame tells me how many males, females or undertermined individuals I have at size, say, 25. I attach  a subset of the data. My questions are:  1) being number of individuals (noind) the variable I need to plot, can I indicate in the command that lgntclass is the bin, or do I have to enter that information adding a binwidth and bin range? I have gone through lots of your examples but cannot find the answer. And, 2) does the data format matter, should I further aggregate the data  (the example I attached are the measurings registered in each sample)?

Thanks for your help,

Elena

 # Or if you want to be fancy, maybe even this: 
> ggplot(diamonds, aes(price, fill = cut)) + 
+   geom_density(alpha = 0.2)

--

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: length frequency by sex with ggplot2
parts:
Elena,

You will need to change the structure of your data a little.  The example you show uses geom_density which expects your data to have one row for each individual.  In the diamonds data, that means each row contains the price and cut of a single diamond, in your data you will need each row to contain the sex and length class of a single fish.  This is easily obtained by duplicating the sex and class of each row of your data by the number of individuals observed:

fish <- read.csv("~/Downloads/test.txt")

# unsummarise: one row for each individual
fish_unsummary <- with(fish, data.frame(X = rep(X, noind), 
  sex = rep(sex, noind), year = rep(year, noind),
  lgntclass = rep(lgntclass, noind) ))    

qplot(lgntclass, data = fish_unsummary, geom = "density", fill = sex,
  alpha = I(0.3))

An alternative to the density estimate is to plot frequency polygons for your data.  In that case you would summarise the counts over all samples.

# summarise further: sum each class over all samples
fish_summary <- ddply(fish, c("lgntclass", "sex"), summarise,
  total_ind = sum(noind))
  
qplot(lgntclass, total_ind, data = fish_summary, geom = "polygon", fill = sex,
  alpha = I(0.3))

Hope that helps,
Charlotte
